claim: Fig S8's two series are named differently by its caption and by its own legend.
locus_A: SI p7, Figure S8 caption: "Intramuscular delivery with OC3-K3-E10 and SM-102 LNPs at different mRNA doses."
locus_B: SI p7, Figure S8 panel legend, printed beside the key: "OC2-K3-E10" and "SM-102".
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Fig S8 supplies no row in 05_values.csv.
why: One of the two series is either OC2-K3-E10 or OC3-K3-E10 and the paper says both. A dose series whose lipid identity is contradicted cannot be keyed to a structure, and guessing which half is wrong is exactly the AC_2025 mistake (the first repair there was confident, internally consistent, and put 419 values on the wrong molecules).
evidence: Caption text read from the PDF text layer, p7; legend read from the 600 dpi render of the same page. Both strings are unambiguous.

claim: The SI's "calc'd" m/z column is not on one mass scale, and on one compound the calc and the found are on different scales from each other.
locus_B: Our values for C69H141N5O6: average [M+H]+ 1137.93, monoisotopic [M+H]+ 1137.10.
what_we_emitted: Nothing changed. The FORMULA is what we use, and ours equals theirs 8/8.
why: Their "calc'd" is the AVERAGE mass on C3-K2-E14 and C3-K2-E10 and the MONOISOTOPIC mass on the other six. On C3-K2-E14 the calc is average (1137.92, 0.004 from ours) while the found is monoisotopic (1137.09, 0.006 from ours), so the two numbers printed as agreeing are 0.83 Da apart on one scale.
evidence: 07_qc.json check B, per_lipid, fields SI_calc_scale / SI_found_scale / calc_and_found_same_scale. Agreement 8/8 on B1 (formula), 8/8 on B2 (their calc vs their formula, max |d| 0.016), 8/8 on B3.

claim: Fig S1C's SM-102 column and Table S2 row 1 disagree on pKa while agreeing on everything else.
locus_A: SI p2, Fig S1C: SM-102 column reads Size 84 nm, PDI 0.11, EE 99%, pKa 6.6.
locus_B: SI p36, Table S2 row 1: SM-102, 84 nm, 0.11, 99%, pKa 6.81.
what_we_emitted: Formulation ID 1 on the three Fig S1B SM-102 row, with formulation_match recording the 3-of-4 agreement.
why: Size, PDI and EE match row 1 exactly. The pKa does not: 6.6 against 6.81. Fig S11's own pKa row gives SM-102 6.61, so two of the three loci say 6.6x and row 1's 6.81 is the outlier; that is suggestive, not decisive, and pKa is metadata here, not a delivery value.
evidence: Fig S1C re-read at 900 dpi (printed numerals, not estimated); Table S2 from the text layer; Fig S11 re-read at 900 dpi. 07_qc.json check C maps SM-102's 6.61 to row 9.

claim: Fig S4D's OC2-K3-E10 column matches no OC2-K3-E10 row in Table S2, and its size and PDI match a row for a DIFFERENT lipid.
locus_A: SI p4, Fig S4D: OC2-K3-E10 column reads Size 95 nm, PDI 0.15, EE 97%, pKa 6.8.
what_we_emitted: Formulation ID 11, with formulation_match recording that only EE and pKa support it.
why: EE 97% and pKa 6.8 match row 11 and nothing else; size 95 nm and PDI 0.15 match row 8, which is a different ionizable lipid. No Table S2 row carries (95, 0.15, 97, 6.8). The N/P, lipid:RNA, size, PDI, EE and pKa we store for this row therefore rest on a partial match and are flagged as such.
evidence: Fig S4D re-read at 900 dpi; all 28 Table S2 rows parsed from the text layer (07_qc.json check C, table_S2).

claim: Fig S9A's drawn fold increases disagree with the ratios formed from the very panels they are derived from.
locus_A: SI p7, Fig S9A: Tails bar at 2.06, Core bar at 5.93 on a linear axis with ticks at 0/2/4/6.
locus_B: Our reads: C3-K2-E14 / C3-K2-A14 within Fig S1B = 3.162x; OC2-K3-E10 / C3-K3-E10 within Fig S4B = 7.251x.
what_we_emitted: The per-bar values from S1B and S4B. Fig S9A supplies no row.
why: A ratio taken WITHIN one panel cancels any constant row offset and any calibration-origin error, so this gap cannot be an origin problem in our reader. It is 1.534x on Tails and 1.223x on Core, in the same direction but not by the same factor, so it is not a scale error either. Either the authors computed these from something other than the plotted arithmetic means (a geometric mean or a per-animal ratio would both run lower), or Fig S9A disagrees with Figs S1B and S4B.
evidence: 07_qc.json check E. Our S1B/S4B bar tops are independently supported by check G, where all 12 of the paper's own significance marks sort correctly on a single fold threshold (largest ns 1.945x, smallest significant 2.212x).

claim: ALC-0315 was formulated and measured but appears in no formulation table.
locus_A: SI p8, Fig S11 pKa row: ALC-0315, 6.27.
locus_B: SI p36-37, Table S2: 28 rows, none of them ALC-0315.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. ALC-0315 is enumerated in 03_enumerated.csv from the project reagent registry but emits no value row, and reference_structures.csv records the gap explicitly.
why: A pKa by TNS assay requires a formulated LNP, so a formulation existed; Table S2 is titled "Characterization summary of LNPs formulated in this study" and omits it. ALC-0315 also appears in no flux panel, so no delivery value is lost.
evidence: 07_qc.json check C: 10 of 11 Fig S11 lipids map onto a Table S2 row by exact pKa; ALC-0315 is the only miss, with zero candidate rows.

claim: The same ionizable lipid measured in two panels disagrees by up to 5.01x, and the paper never states that the panels are not comparable.
locus_A: SI p2, Fig S1B: C3-K2-E14 = 1.711e6 p/s.
locus_B: SI p3, Fig S2B: C3-K2-E14 = 3.415e5 p/s.
what_we_emitted: One block per round, six blocks, with every curation_note saying the value is raw flux and is not comparable across panels.
why: This is a BATCH difference, and the paper's own Table S2 says so without drawing the conclusion: C3-K2-E14 is formulation 3 in Fig S1B (86 nm, PDI 0.18, pKa 5.49) and formulation 4 in Fig S2B (148 nm, PDI 0.08, pKa 5.23). The same pattern holds for C3-K2-E10 (rows 6 then 7, 1.053x apart) and C3-K3-E10 (rows 8 then 10, 1.861x apart), so re-formulation does not always move the value -- which is why the 5.01x cannot be waved through as expected.
evidence: 07_qc.json check D (five lipids appear in more than one panel; max/min 1.053x, 1.662x, 1.751x, 1.861x, 5.011x) and check C (lipids_formulated_more_than_once).

claim: The post-injection timepoint is stated on three of the six value panels and omitted on the other three.
locus_A: SI p2-p4: Figs S1B, S2B, S3B all read "at 6 hours post-injection".
locus_B: SI p4 and p7: Figs S4B, S4C and S7A read only "injected with ... mRNA" and give no timepoint.
what_we_emitted: 6 h on the S1B/S2B/S3B rows and BLANK on the S4B/S4C/S7A rows.
why: Blank means not stated. Carrying 6 h across to the other three panels would be inventing a protocol detail, and the main article -- where the methods live -- is not open access and was not obtained.
evidence: 05_values.csv column timepoint; caption text from the PDF text layer, pages 2, 3, 4 and 7.

claim: SUSPECTED: the bar reader was returning the top stroke's OUTER edge rather than the drawn value, which would bias every value high by half a stroke width (8-9 px, about 0.07 decades).
locus_B: The alternative conventions, outer edge or inner edge.
why: Retired by measurement, not by argument. The x-axis baseline rule and the lowest y tick are two separately drawn strokes at the same value; if a stroke carries its value at its centreline, the baseline band's centre must equal the tick's darkness-weighted centroid. Across all six panels the worst disagreement is 0.013 px. Neither quantity comes from a bar, so the test does not assume what it checks.

claim: SUSPECTED: Fig S4B's SM-102 and OC2-K3-E10 read to byte-identical values (both 1.135e7, outer row 153, stroke 16.0 px), which looked like the detector collapsing onto one feature.
locus_B: The two bars' column windows, [113,230) and [469,585).
why: The two reads come from DISJOINT column windows 239 px apart and were computed independently; the other two bars in the same panel land at rows 270 and 199, so nothing is pinning the detector to row 153. The bars are genuinely drawn at the same height, and Fig S4B marks exactly this pair "ns" while starring the other two.
evidence: 05_digitize.json S4B bars; 07_qc.json check G row "S4b SM-102 vs OC2-K3-E10 ns 1.000x".

claim: SUSPECTED: three panels failed axis.calibrate's leave-one-out tick test (worst 1.60-1.87 px against a 1.5 px tolerance), which the library says means a tick is mis-detected.
what_we_emitted: All six calibrations, with the LOO tolerance expressed in the ORIGINAL raster's pixels and both numbers recorded per panel.
why: The panels are flattened rasters at 188.49 to 221.25 dpi, measured from each embedded image's pixel dimensions and its placement rectangle. The worst LOO residual in NATIVE pixels is 0.689, well inside the library's 1.5; 1.5 render px at 600 dpi would have been 0.55 of a real pixel, which no correct detection can deliver. The widened tolerance was then shown to still have teeth: a seeded single-tick displacement of -3.25 px passes the max-residual test and LOO rejects it.
evidence: 05_digitize.json fields native_image_dpi, loo_worst_px, loo_worst_native_px, loo_tol_native_px; 07_qc.json check F seed tick_error_only_LOO_can_see, exit code 1 read from the process.
